title: Every Face of the Die
statement: You roll a fair six-sided die until every face has appeared at least once. What is the expected number of rolls?
insight: Split the wait into phases: after seeing k faces, the wait for a new one is geometric with success probability (6−k)/6.
redHerring: Trying to compute the probability that all faces have appeared within n rolls and summing tails.
hints: Break the process into stages by how many distinct faces you have seen.
Once you have seen $k$ faces, what is the chance the next roll is new?
A geometric wait with success probability $p$ has mean $1/p$.
solution:
After $k$ distinct faces, each roll is new with probability $\tfrac{6-k}{6}$, so that phase lasts $\tfrac{6}{6-k}$ rolls on average.

Total: $6\left(\tfrac16+\tfrac15+\tfrac14+\tfrac13+\tfrac12+1\right) = 6\cdot 2.45 = 14.7$.
